subject: PrivateStack IaC: module interface linter and CI safety net
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Will Harris <will.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, os-advisor@netops-llc.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivateStack IaC: module interface linter and CI safety net

Team / Will,

Summary: we want to establish a lightweight, enforceable linter and CI safety net for Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules that ship into Acme's privatestack. Goal is to catch interface/inputs drift, require minimal churn for reviewers, and provide an automatic canary flow to validate changes in a staging enclave before production promotion.

What I'm asking for in this thread:
- Review the proposed lint rules (attached) for false positives / exceptions.
- Confirm the gating jobs we plan to wire into GitLab (names below).
- Validate the canary runbook and owners: who owns the smoke validation and rapid rollback.

Key constraints:
- Some older modules in their repo are pinned to legacy providers; we need exceptions for a short window.
- Network changes are sensitive; any Terraform changes touching VPC peering / BGP must route an immediate pager and include a rollback plan.
- We must not block small ansible/helm value bumps (image tags) with full terraform plans unless they touch infra interfaces.

Attachments: module-interface-linter.yml; gitlab-ci-privatestack-example.yml; priv-iac-canary-runbook.md

Proposed GitLab jobs (names):
- lint/module-interface-check
- ci/plan-verify (non-blocking for minor modules)
- ci/gate-canary-deploy
- ci/rollback-verify

Next: Vivek / Lauren please comment on the CI job semantics and who will own the runbook steps. Will / NetOps: please call out any network review gating you'd like added.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrivateStack IaC: module interface linter and CI safety net

Thanks, Kimberly. Appreciate the clear ask. A few clarifications from Acme SRE side:

1) Legacy module exceptions:
We have ~12 modules that still reference v2 of the private-provider. We can accept an opt-out label on the MR for up to 90 days, but we need a ticket per-module with remediation ETA and the exemption must be visible in the merge summary. Can your linter surface a required ticket ID if it detects the legacy provider?

2) Network change gating:
Any MR that touches aws_vpc, aws_route_table, or any BGP peering resource must include a JSON payload with the expected IP/ASN delta and run the staging-bgp-sim job. We require the job to emit a diff artifact we can inspect. If that's not producible, we won't approve the MR.

3) Canary ownership and pager:
Who will be on-call for the canary deployment window? For us, the default will be Acme SRE primary on weekdays; we can make exceptions for weekend schedules. If Redwood wants to trigger a canary outside our on-call, please coordinate 48 hours in advance.

I took a quick look at the linter YAML — a few rules look aggressive on variable naming (e.g., forbidding camelCase in outputs). Can we allow an exceptions list per-module?

Will
Will Harris
SRE Manager, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: PrivateStack IaC: module interface linter and CI safety net

Kimberly / team / Will —

Thanks for the input; quick implementation sketch from the CI side (GitLab):

1) Linter job (lint/module-interface-check)- runs module-interface-linter.yml as a container step; exits non-zero only if a rule hits "block" severity. We will allow per-module exceptions via a .module-lint-ignore file checked in the MR. The linter binary will accept a --require-ticket flag that fails if a legacy-provider pattern is found without a ticket reference.

2) Plan-verify (ci/plan-verify)- runs terraform plan with workspace=staging and uses a small policy-check container to classify changes as network/infrastructure/metadata. Network/infra changes will be annotated in the MR (artifact: plan-classification.json).

3) Canary-deploy (ci/gate-canary-deploy)- triggered automatically for infra changes that pass plan-verify; deploys to a short-lived staging enclave (ttl=2h). Canary job will: deploy, run smoke tests (tcp/icmp/health endpoints), run bgp-sim if BGP touched, and post a summary artifact with healthcheck logs. Canary-deploy will be non-blocking by default but will create a manual approval step if classification shows BGP or VPC changes.

4) Rollback-verify (ci/rollback-verify)- runs the destroy path in isolated namespace and validates the cluster returns to baseline. This job will be manual approval gated.

Config notes:
- We will expose a lint severity matrix in the shared drive and default to warn for style failures and block for interface/schema drift.
- Exceptions per-module will be a short file with a ticket link; the linter will surface missing links as a CI failure when --require-ticket is enabled.

Attachments: gitlab-ci-privatestack-example.yml (contains job templates and artifact handling).

Action: I can drop a draft pipeline MR by EOD Monday with job templates for you to review. Vivek / Irene / Karthik: please confirm the ttl and staging enclave sizing assumptions.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Will / team —

Thanks for the thoughtful responses. Quick decisions and next steps from Redwood: 

Decisions: 1) We will enable --require-ticket in the linter for legacy-provider detection. Linter will fail and annotate the MR unless a valid ticket ID is present in the MR description. 2) Any change that touches VPC/BGP will trigger the manual approval step in ci/gate-canary-deploy; Acme SRE will be set as the default approver during their on-call window. 3) Per-module exceptions are allowed via .module-lint-ignore but must point to a tracked remediation ticket that has an ETA. Exceptions expire after 90 days automatically.

Action items: 
- Lauren: create draft MR with pipeline templates and the example lint config (INFRA-2143) — target: 2026-10-12 EOD.
- Vivek / Irene: confirm staging enclave sizing and give a short runbook comment on the smoke checks — target: 2026-10-13 noon.
- Will: provide the preferred on-call rotation for canary approvals and the JSON format for the IP/ASN delta (Will suggested a small schema).
- Karthik: add a short terraform plan classifier to the shared artifact pipeline (work item: add classifier to plan-verify).
- Procurement: procurement@acme-corp.com — we'll need a short MSA addendum for the canary resource usage (cc'ed).

I've uploaded the runbook draft and linked a Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2143. If there are no objections by EOD Tuesday I'll merge the MR and schedule a canary window for Wednesday 2026-10-14 09:00-11:00 PT.
